title: Agent-Based Discrete-Event Simulation Modelling of Metro Stations for Crowd Management and Passenger Flow Analysis
content: Metro systems have become increasingly crucial components of sustainable urban mo-bility solutions. The effectiveness of metro systems, however, depends on station ca-pacity and passenger behaviour within stations is a recurring and constantly evolving challenge. Efficient crowd management in metro stations is therefore a critical chal-lenge for transport operators due to increasing passenger demand and the need to maintain safe and reliable operations. Using a combination of agent-based modelling and discrete-event simulation, this study develops an integrated simulation frame-work, and applies to two typical metro stations, De Ferrari Station in Genoa, Italy, and Serdica Station in Sofia, Bulgaria, using Simul8 – an event-based simulation modelling software. The models represent passenger and train interactions within station envi-ronments, including inbound, outbound and transferring passenger movements, ticket purchasing and validation activities, utilisation of stairways, escalators and elevators and train boarding and alighting processes. Passenger behaviour is modelled through a combination of specific routings, queuing and stochastic activity durations provided by data from metro operators, site observations and local knowledge. Validation was undertaken by comparing simulated passenger flows against observed data at key sta-tion locations, including entrances, platforms, concourses, and transfer areas. Results demonstrate a high level of accuracy, with simulated flows closely mirroring observed values for both stations. Findings confirm that the integrated simulation framework provides a robust and effective approach for analysing station operations, identifying congestion points, and supporting evidence-based decision-making for station design and crowd management improvements.
